<implementation-notes>
IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
This feature adds Grype vulnerability scanning as a step between SBOM generation (CC-0029) and SBOM attestation in the supply chain pipeline. The full chain becomes: build → push → SBOM → **Grype scan** → attest → sign.

**Critical design decision — Grype runs on BOTH push and PR:** Unlike SBOM generation, attestation, and cosign signing (which are guarded by `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`), Grype scan steps have NO PR guard. This is intentional: PRs need fail-fast feedback on high-severity CVEs. The input source differs: push uses SBOM file (faster, offline-capable), PR uses image directly (since SBOM is not generated on PRs).

**Conditional input wiring:** Each Grype step uses GitHub Actions ternary expressions to set either `sbom:` (push) or `image:` (PR) input, with the other set to empty string. The `anchore/grype-action` treats empty string inputs as unset. For base images on PR, the image is referenced by digest from GHCR (base images are always pushed). For service images on PR, the image is referenced by the composite tag from `steps.tags.outputs.composite` (service images use `load: true` on PRs).

**SARIF upload with `if: always()`:** When Grype detects high/critical CVEs, it exits non-zero (due to `fail-on: high`), which would skip subsequent steps. The SARIF upload step uses `if: always()` to ensure results are uploaded to the GitHub Security tab even when vulnerabilities are found. This is critical — without it, SARIF would only be uploaded when NO high-severity CVEs exist.

**Step IDs for output wiring:** Grype steps need `id:` fields (grype-python-base, grype-venv-builder, grype-service) so SARIF upload steps can reference `${{ steps.<id>.outputs.sarif }}` for the SARIF file path.

**SHA resolution:** The implementer must look up current SHAs for `anchore/grype-action` (latest commit on v0 branch/tag) and `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` (latest commit on v3 branch/tag) from GitHub. Use the same SHA consistently across all steps of each action.

**Key files:**
- `.github/workflows/build-images.yaml` — main workflow (lines 36-175 for base images, 211-398 for service images)
- `.grype.yaml` — new config file at repo root
- `tests/container-images/verify_build_images_workflow.sh` — workflow structure tests (add after CC-0030 tests around line 1140)
- `tests/lib/assertions.sh` — shared assertion helpers (read-only, not modified)
- `docs/reference/build-images-workflow.md` — reference documentation

**Risks:** (1) anchore/grype-action version may have breaking changes — mitigated by SHA pinning. (2) Grype DB download on every run adds ~10-15s — acceptable for security benefit, not worth caching (YAGNI). (3) False positives may block builds — mitigated by .grype.yaml ignore list. (4) SARIF upload may fail on fork PRs due to missing security-events permission — mitigated by existing fork PR rejection step.
</implementation-notes>

<go-testing-patterns>
    <pattern name="table-driven-tests">
      Use table-driven tests ([]struct with name, input, expected fields) for functions with multiple input/output combinations.
      Each sub-test via t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) { ... }) for clear failure isolation.
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="test-helpers">
      Use t.Helper() in shared test helper functions so failures report the caller's line number.
      Use t.Cleanup() for teardown instead of defer when cleanup must run after subtests.
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="testify-assertions">
      Prefer testify assert/require for readable assertions: require.NoError, assert.Equal, assert.Contains.
      Use require (fatal) for preconditions, assert (non-fatal) for actual checks.
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="test-file-conventions">
      Test files: *_test.go in the same package (white-box) or _test package (black-box).
      Test functions: TestFunctionName, TestType_MethodName. Subtests via t.Run for variants.
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="mocking">
      Use interfaces for dependencies, inject test doubles. Prefer hand-written fakes over mock frameworks.
      For HTTP: httptest.NewServer. For filesystem: testing/fstest or os.MkdirTemp with t.TempDir().
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="go-test-commands">
      Run tests: go test ./... | Verbose: go test -v ./... | Coverage: go test -cover ./...

  <purpose>Condensed language-agnostic rules for production-quality code</purpose>

  <section name="error-handling">
    <rule id="ERR-1">NEVER return sentinel values (None, -1, empty string) to indicate errors — raise/return an error</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-2">Chain or wrap exceptions to preserve the original cause and stack trace</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-3">Catch the most specific exception type possible — never bare except/catch-all</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-4">Include context in error messages: what operation failed, with which inputs, and why</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-5">Never silently swallow exceptions — log + re-raise, or handle explicitly</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="architecture">
    <rule id="ARCH-1">Services orchestrate workflows — no business logic in controllers/handlers, no HTTP/CLI concerns in services</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-2">Repositories return domain objects, not ORM models or raw dicts</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-3">Domain layer has zero imports from infrastructure, API, or framework code</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-4">Use dependency injection — pass dependencies as constructor/function parameters, never import and instantiate inline</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-5">One function, one responsibility — if you describe a function with "and", split it</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="async-concurrency">
    <rule id="ASYNC-1">NEVER call blocking I/O (file reads, HTTP requests, sleep) inside async functions — use async equivalents or run in a thread pool</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-2">Use the language-appropriate wrapper for unavoidable blocking code in async contexts (run_in_executor, goroutines, worker threads)</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-3">Never fire-and-forget async tasks — always await, collect, or track them for error handling</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-4">Use async-safe primitives for shared state — async locks, channels, or atomic operations</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-5">Limit concurrency for external calls with semaphores or worker pools — unbounded parallelism causes resource exhaustion</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="data-modeling">
    <rule id="DATA-1">Use the simplest appropriate type — plain function before class, flat struct before nested hierarchy</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-2">Use immutable types for value objects — frozen dataclasses, readonly structs, Object.freeze</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-3">Validate at system boundaries (API input, config loading, file parsing) — trust internal data</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-4">Prefer enums over string constants for fixed sets of values — catches typos at compile/import time</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="resource-management">
    <rule id="RES-1">Use context managers, defer, try-finally, or using blocks for ALL resources (files, connections, locks, temp files)</rule>
    <rule id="RES-2">Clean up partial state on failure — delete created files, rollback transactions, release reservations</rule>
    <rule id="RES-3">Set explicit timeouts on ALL external calls (HTTP, database, queues) — no call should block indefinitely</rule>
  </section>

## Description

Integration tests that depend on envtest use the single, centralized exported `SkipIfEnvTestUnavailable` helper from the `envtest` package. It checks both the KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS env var and the presence of the etcd binary. Tests using the `//go:build integration` tag separate integration tests from unit tests. // SkipIfEnvTestUnavailable skips the calling test if the KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS

func SkipIfEnvTestUnavailable(t testing.TB) {

	}
}

## Description

RunJob guards against stale completed Jobs by comparing existing.Spec.Template.Spec against the desired job.Spec.Template.Spec using apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual after confirming IsJobComplete. When specs differ (e.g., new container image from an operator upgrade), the old Job is deleted and a new one is created with the updated spec, returning (false, nil) so the reconciler requeues. This prevents silently skipping migrations when the operator binary changes.

Instead of maintaining a normalization layer that mirrors API-server defaulting logic (fragile and requires updates with every Kubernetes version), a SHA-256 hash of the desired spec is stored as an annotation at creation time.
